summary: ACL cutover Phase-3 (cinatra#1898, epic #1883 §D7; product decision 2026-07-20 'ruling 5': a dashboard is ALWAYS visible to everyone in its scope) — DROP the demoted `dashboards.visibility` column. ONE destructive DDL step, ALTER TABLE dashboards DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS visibility; the column's CHECK (dashboards_visibility_check plus the inline CREATE-time CHECK) rides the column drop automatically, so no separate DROP CONSTRAINT is issued. RESTRICT (the default) is deliberate: a dependent index/view/generated column fails the ALTER loudly instead of being CASCADE-dropped. SAFE NOW because Phase-2 (PR #2064, merged) replaced the dashboard-local ACL internals AND the library's dual authorization with ONE canonical resolver — access derives purely from scope (owner_level/owner_id + the project_id refinement), the row projection of the canonical object.read filter — and core__0082 converged every dashboard twin's objects tuple onto that mapping; the column has been WRITE-ONLY since, with no read path, filter, index or view, so the drop removes dead storage rather than an authorization input. The demoted column is the ONLY one dropped: owner_level/owner_id are NOT demoted (they are the scope axis the canonical mapping reads and additionally back the per-entity identity composite of #700 and its unique indexes); dashboard_revisions is kept per ruling 5; cube DATA authorization (SecurityContext visibility resolvers) is a different subsystem and is untouched. The operator-upgrade twin of the fresh-install bootstrap shape in src/lib/drizzle-store.ts (the `dashboards` CREATE loses the visibility column and its idempotent CHECK DO-block, spread in the SAME PR): a fresh install bootstraps the post-drop shape and ledger-fakes the chain, an existing deployment executes this module at boot / `cinatra db migrate`. Idempotent (DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS is a no-op once gone); unqualified names ride the runner's search_path; metadata-only DDL, no noTransaction(). A fail-loud postcondition asserts the column is absent from information_schema.columns for the current schema, so a partial or skipped apply RAISEs and rolls back. down() restores the column SHAPE (visibility text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'private' + its CHECK) so a rollback to a Phase-2-era image, which writes the column on every insert but never reads it, keeps working — HONEST COST: original per-row values are NOT recoverable (every row returns at the 'private' default); a rollback PAST Phase-2 to code that still authorizes on visibility is not supported by this pair (core__0082 is itself irreversible, so the cutover is a one-way door); restore from a backup if the original values are genuinely required. SEQ 0087 — strictly greater than the max seq on live origin/main (core__0086_dependency-edge-declared-role) and greater than every seq claimed by an open PR at authoring time (no open PR carries a migrations/core/ module); seq is assigned at MERGE, so a rename-only renumber of this module plus this fragment is normal if a concurrent lane lands first (the runner tolerates gaps). migrations/** is HIGH-RISK: owner approval required; the lane never merges.
